stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They hypothesized that whether a small request came first would affect compliance with a large request.

**Participants.** The sample was 120 homeowners, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

**Results.** The group that was first asked to sign the petition: agreed to display the sign (%) = 55. The group that was only asked to display the sign: agreed to display the sign (%) = 18. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: After a study in which participants were misled about its purpose, the researcher explains what was really being studied. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.
Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Correct. Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.explanation: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress?

options.why: Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also test hypotheses.
Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: A therapist asks a client to explain what her symptoms mean in her culture rather than assuming he already knows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Correct. Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.explanation: Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive appraisal?

options.text: The theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources
options.why: That describes the broaden-and-build theory.

options.text: A cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom
options.why: That describes a display rule.

options.text: The interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive appraisal means.

options.text: An event or stimulus that triggers an emotion
options.why: That describes an elicitor.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: Aaron spends his weekends skydiving and rock climbing. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Correct. Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that working memory span causes a change in reading comprehension score?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: After being asked several times to imagine spilling punch at a wedding as a child, a student becomes confident it really happened. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Correct. Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.explanation: Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.

questions.stem: In psychodynamic theory, denial, projection and rationalization are all examples of which of the following?

options.why: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance?

options.why: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.
Correct. Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.explanation: Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members?

options.why: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
Correct. Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron?

options.why: Correct. The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.

questions.explanation: The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.

questions.stem: Ben always plans ahead, meets every deadline and keeps his desk tidy. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Correct. Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.explanation: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.stem: Lena is so terrified of spiders that she will not enter any room where she has ever seen one. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes eustress?

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: That describes health psychology.

options.text: The positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge
options.why: Correct. This is what eustress means.

options.text: The response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support
options.why: That describes the tend-and-befriend response.

options.text: The response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape
options.why: That describes the fight-or-flight response.

questions.explanation: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.stem: On one day, a researcher gives the same memory test to groups of 20-, 40- and 60-year-olds and compares them. Which research design is this?

options.why: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.
Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.
Correct. A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.explanation: A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes emotion-focused coping?

options.text: Persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress
options.why: That describes hypertension.

options.text: The reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it
options.why: That describes problem-focused coping.

options.text: The reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor
options.why: Correct. This is what emotion-focused coping means.

options.text: The weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress
options.why: That describes immune suppression.

questions.explanation: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in attention to the road at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: The phone group drove a more difficult route in the simulator
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in phone use
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits?

options.why: The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.
Correct. Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.
Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.

questions.explanation: Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Heroin belongs to which category of psychoactive drugs?

options.why: Correct. An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes epigenetics?

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nurture.

options.text: The study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself
options.why: Correct. This is what epigenetics means.

options.text: Research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives
options.why: That describes an adoption study.

questions.explanation: Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.

questions.stem: Girls reminded of the stereotype that girls are bad at math just before a math test score lower than girls who are not reminded. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Correct. Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.

questions.explanation: Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: This is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Shoppers prefer beef labeled '80% lean' to the same beef labeled '20% fat'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.
The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.
Correct. Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.explanation: Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity?

options.why: Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: Tess remembers the number 177618652001 by treating it as three famous years. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Correct. Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.explanation: Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness?

options.why: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
Correct. The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.

questions.explanation: The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.stem: A two-year-old insists, 'Me do it!' when getting dressed. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: A charity first asks people to sign a petition and a week later asks the same people for a donation. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: A witness picks the thief out of a line-up of six people. Which measure of memory is this?

options.why: Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Correct. Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.
A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.explanation: Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards?

options.why: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Correct. A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.
Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.

questions.explanation: A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.stem: On a very easy test, most students score near 100 but a few score very low, so the mean is below the median. Which shape does the distribution have?

options.why: The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.
The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
Correct. A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment?

options.why: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Correct. Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.

questions.stem: During adolescence, the reproductive organs themselves mature. These organs are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes positive punishment?

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes positive reinforcement.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: Correct. This is what positive punishment means.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes negative punishment.

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes negative reinforcement.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time?

options.why: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Correct. Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.explanation: Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.

questions.stem: After a head injury, Amir can learn new things but cannot remember anything from the year before the accident. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Correct. Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes hoarding disorder?

options.text: An unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety
options.why: That describes an obsession.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic stress disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered
options.why: Correct. This is what hoarding disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times
options.why: That describes dissociative identity disorder.

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.75. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: A four-year-old enjoys pretend play and talks well, but thinks a tall glass holds more juice than a wide glass with the same amount. Which of Piaget's stages is he in?

options.why: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
Correct. The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.stem: Although she was not listening, Bea can repeat the last few words her teacher just said. Which kind of memory makes this possible?

options.why: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Correct. Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.explanation: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sublimation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: Correct. This is what sublimation means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A medication prevents the sending neuron from taking serotonin back, so more serotonin stays in the synapse. The medication is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: A therapist teaches a client to challenge her anxious thoughts and also gives her homework to practice new behaviors. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Correct. Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.

questions.explanation: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables?

options.why: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
Correct. A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.explanation: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles?

options.why: Correct. The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.
The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.explanation: The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.

questions.stem: A person notices when 1 kg is added to a 10 kg load but needs 5 kg to be added before noticing a change in a 50 kg load. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Correct. Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
The just-noticeable difference is the smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.explanation: Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.

questions.stem: Bored on a quiet afternoon, Raj goes looking for something exciting to do, although all his physical needs are met. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Correct. Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.explanation: Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.stem: A signal leaves Tia's spinal cord and makes her arm muscles contract. Which cells carry this outgoing signal?

options.why: The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Correct. Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.explanation: Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.

questions.stem: Rubbing a bumped elbow reduces the pain because the touch signals close off the pain signals in the spinal cord. Which theory explains this?

options.why: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Correct. The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.stem: To read small print, a person moves their eyes so the words fall on the point of sharpest vision. What is this point called?

options.why: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
Correct. The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.explanation: The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.stem: The group that took practice quizzes scored higher. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The study method caused the difference in memory for a passage
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The study method and memory for a passage are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park is slower than he used to be at solving unfamiliar logic puzzles. Which kind of intelligence has declined?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Correct. Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.

questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the unconditioned stimulus?

options.text: In classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning
options.why: Correct. This is what the unconditioned stimulus means.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus
options.why: That describes the unconditioned response.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus
options.why: That describes the conditioned response.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus
options.why: That describes the conditioned stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: Fourteen-year-old Jo refuses to go to school because she is sure everyone will stare at the small spot on her chin. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.
The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.
The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.

questions.explanation: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that did gentle stretching
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an approach-approach conflict?

options.text: The desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying
options.why: That describes intrinsic motivation.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options
options.why: Correct. This is what an approach-approach conflict means.

options.text: A conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features
options.why: That describes an approach-avoidance conflict.

options.text: The desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment
options.why: That describes extrinsic motivation.

questions.explanation: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes acquisition?

options.text: The reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period
options.why: That describes spontaneous recovery.

options.text: The learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli
options.why: That describes stimulus discrimination.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned
options.why: Correct. This is what acquisition means.

options.text: The pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus
options.why: That describes higher-order conditioning.

questions.explanation: Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 5, 8, 8, 10, 4, 17, 11. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (63) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 4, 5, 8, 8, 10, 11, 17. Add the scores (63) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (9) above the median (8), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Without evidence, Hugo is convinced that his coworkers, neighbors and friends are all plotting against him, and he has felt this way for years. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes texture gradient?

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer
options.why: That describes interposition.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away
options.why: Correct. This is what texture gradient means.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones
options.why: That describes relative clarity.

options.text: The binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes
options.why: That describes retinal disparity.

questions.explanation: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.

questions.stem: At six months, a baby says 'da-da-da' and 'ma-ma-ma' without meaning anything by it. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Correct. Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.explanation: Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.stem: Researchers find that a person who collapses is helped more quickly when one person is nearby than when a crowd is nearby. What is this finding called?

options.why: Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Correct. The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.explanation: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter increases alertness and arousal as part of the body's response to stress?

options.why: Correct. Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse?

options.why: Correct. Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
The threshold is the level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are below 80?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is below.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is below. (80 and 120 are one standard deviation from the mean; 60 and 140 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of compliance with a large request

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of compliance with a large request.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Compliance with a large request was defined as the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. On average, the value was 55 for the group that was first asked to sign the petition and 18 for the group that was only asked to display the sign, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 120 homeowners from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. (55 compared with 18).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that whether a small request came first affects compliance with a large request. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to whether a small request came first. The finding illustrates the foot-in-the-door technique: agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a larger one, partly to stay consistent and avoid cognitive dissonance.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
